reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Genesis 2's shrub and herb of the field as the later cultivated growth requiring rain and tillage, not the day-three vegetation of Genesis 1.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen reads the Yahwist's creation order as systematically different from the Priestly scheme, of which this plant-before-human sequence is one instance.

quotes.text: Jehovah Himself puts His hand to the work, and this supposes that the world in its main features was already in existence. He plants and waters the garden, He forms man and breathes life into his nostrils, He builds the woman out of the man's rib, having made a previous attempt, which was unsuccessful, to provide him with company; the beasts are living witnesses of the failure of His experiments.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the Yahwist's order of creative acts in the two Genesis accounts.

sides.snippet: The earth brought forth grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, with its seed in it, after their kind: and God saw that it was good.
sides.verseText: The earth brought forth grass, herbs yielding seed after their kind, and trees bearing fruit, with its seed in it, after their kind: and God saw that it was good.

sides.snippet: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food
sides.verseText: Out of the ground Yahweh God made every tree to grow that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
